bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in India's abrasives industry with the widest product range (one of only two full-range players)
- Backward integration via Saint-Gobain's Ceramic Materials Division, which manufactures high-end abrasive grains
- Access to Saint-Gobain's global R&D centres (including a Centre in India) and Centers of Excellence
- Deep customer connect, ability to customise solutions, and brand equity built over decades
- Broad-based industry exposure in Abrasives — dependence on any single industry segment is less than 15%, insulating the business from segment-specific volatility
- Extensive domestic distribution network plus growing non-engineering channels and export diversification
- Digital transformation: in-house-built end-to-end CRM platform, channel partner portal/app, and Industry 4.0 investments improving process efficiency and quality control
- Each PPS sub-business (EQYO, Omniseal Solutions, Life Sciences, Tape Solutions) is a market leader in its space globally and in India
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical demand disruption in PPS end markets — Demand disruption due to geopolitical uncertainty in key markets like Automotive, Life Sciences, Industrial and Oil & Gas is flagged as a major short-term risk for the Performance Polymer Solutions business.
- Raw material availability and input cost inflation — An inflationary environment, concerns over availability of key raw materials, and logistical uncertainties are flagged as critical challenges for the PPS business in the current year; PCR also flags supply chain disruptions and price surcharges on raw materials/energy from ongoing geopolitical tensions.
- Currency risk from import intensity — Depreciation of the Rupee is flagged as a risk specifically because the Performance Polymer Solutions business is import-intensive.
- Import competition and pricing pressure across Abrasives and Silicon Carbide — The Abrasives business faces margin pressure on key high-margin products from global players entering India and rising Chinese imports (power tools accessory range); the Silicon Carbide business faces competition from imports mainly from China, Vietnam and Russia, which kept market prices subdued and pressured margins/volumes during the year.
- Subsidiary performance sensitivity to power/input costs — Saint-Gobain Ceramic Materials Bhutan Private Limited (SGCMBPL), the Company's SiC-manufacturing subsidiary, saw its business subdued during the year on account of increased power and input costs.
- PCR export decline from geopolitical/tariff risk — PCR exports declined during the year due to the uncertain geopolitical situation and the imposition of tariffs in the US.
- Structurally limited growth in Digital Services (INDEC) segment — The captive IT unit operates on a cost-plus model for the Saint-Gobain Group; management states growth in this segment is limited and future growth can happen only on account of cost inflation, and financial performance may be impacted by foreign exchange fluctuation and hedging strategy.
- Competitive intensity from new entrants adjacent to Abrasives — Paint, Adhesives and similar companies entering the Abrasives market with deep distribution and aggressive pricing have been able to penetrate the market quickly, adding to competitive pressure alongside established European/Japanese niche players and Chinese imports.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: GNO manufactures and trades Abrasives (bonded, thin wheels, coated/non-woven, superabrasives, construction products, sealants & adhesives) and, under its Ceramics & Plastics segment, Performance Polymer Solutions (PTFE bearings, seals, life-science tubings, tapes) and Performance Ceramics and Refractories (refractories and engineered ceramics including Silicon Carbide) for customers such as steel, automotive, bearings, general engineering, aerospace, defence, life sciences and construction. It is part of the Saint-Gobain group, drawing on the group's R&D, grain manufacturing (Ceramic Materials Division) and global technology access.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Abrasives:** Bonded Abrasives, Thin Wheels (Cutting/Grinding Wheels), Coated Abrasives, Non-woven Abrasives, Superabrasives (Diamond/CBN), Construction products, Sealants & Adhesives
- **Performance Polymer Solutions (PPS):** EQYO — PTFE Bearings, Yoke Assemblies, precision injection molding components, Omniseal Solutions — Spring Energized Polymer Seals & Metal Seals, Life Sciences — Silicone/TPE Tubings, Single Use Bags & Assemblies, Tape Solutions — EV Tapes & Foams, Pressure Sensitive Adhesive & Acrylic Foam Tapes, Wire Harness tapes, Performance Film Solutions
- **Performance Ceramics and Refractories (PCR):** Refractory products (Tap Hole Clay, Trough & Runner Castables), Engineered ceramics (Silicon impregnated Silicon Carbide, Reaction-bonded Silicon Carbide), Ceramics for Sanitaryware, Tableware, Ballistic Armour Protection, Wear Resistance Systems
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, France — holding: Ultimate holding company, per BRSR and Related Party Transactions disclosure
- Saint-Gobain Ceramic Materials Bhutan Private Limited (SGCMBPL) — subsidiary: 70%-held subsidiary; engaged in manufacture of Silicon Carbide near Phuentsholing, Bhutan; business was subdued during the year on account of increased power and input costs; not a material subsidiary under Regulation 16(1)(c) of Listing Regulations
- Advanced Synthetic Minerals Private Limited (ASMPL) — JV: 49%-held joint venture; during FY2025-26 focused on improving quality and debottlenecking
- Cleanwin Energy Three LLP — associate: 27.27%-held associate; investment for sourcing wind-generated green energy for the Company's Mora Plant, contributing to cost efficiency and sustainability commitments
- Numerous Saint-Gobain group fellow subsidiaries worldwide (e.g. Saint-Gobain India Private Limited, Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics Corporation (US), Saint-Gobain Abrasives entities across China/Thailand/Australia/Europe, Certainteed entities (US/Canada), Saint-Gobain Glass entities (France/UK/Egypt), among many others) — related party: Fellow subsidiaries of ultimate holding company Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, disclosed under Ind AS 24 Related Party Disclosures for related-party transaction purposes

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Abrasives: mitigate pressure on key high-margin products from global players entering India by constantly upgrading products and expanding into new markets and segments
- Abrasives: grow non-engineering channels and diversify into adjacency products, while increasing efforts to grow exports, to partially insulate the business from segment-specific volatility
- Abrasives: continue investing in technology, capacities and capabilities to meet growing competitive challenges from Chinese imports, Paint/Adhesives entrants, and European/Japanese niche players
- PPS: fully aligned to Saint-Gobain Group's 'Lead & Grow' strategy, with five focus areas — growing the business by leveraging capacities & capabilities; competency building for breakthrough solutions; building Application & Product Management expertise; focus on cost, efficiency & working capital via new digital tools; and building stronger processes & enablers for service and growth
- PCR (Secondary Steel): maintain leadership via new products, application engineering techniques and business models focused on increasing throughput and reducing melting cost, including the 'Steel Club' customer engagement/training program
- PCR (Petrochemicals): growth strategy centred on consolidating core offers, selectively expanding into ultra-high-temperature applications, and leveraging India-based manufacturing and engineering capabilities; carbon black remains a key focus area
- SiC: focus on maximising output from both manufacturing locations (Tirupati and Bhutan) along with continued emphasis on price improvement and cost control
- Group-wide: diversified portfolio with continued focus on commercial excellence, innovation, cost competitiveness, productivity, digitalisation and sustainability to sustain profitable growth
- Dividend Distribution Policy objective is to appropriately reward shareholders by sharing a portion of profits while retaining sufficient funds for the Company's growth, balancing dividend payout against profit retention for business utilisation. Before declaring/recommending dividend, the Board considers: profit earned during the financial year, capital expenditure requirements, operating cash flows and treasury position, cash retention for exceptional contingencies, acquisitions or new investments requiring higher capital allocation, higher working capital requirements affecting free cash flow, the external economic environment, and the legal/regulatory framework. The Board may declare interim dividends as it considers fit and recommends final dividend for shareholder approval. Retained earnings are utilised based on expansion plans, diversification, and long-term strategic plans.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Abrasives (Coated segment): commissioning of a new paper maker and a new non-woven line increased production capacity and enhanced the ability to customise products to precise customer specifications. Abrasives (Thin Wheel and Bonded segments): investments in capability building and capacity expansion are already yielding an expanded product range and enhanced innovation capabilities. PCR: engineered ceramics manufacturing capabilities at the Halol plant were expanded with new industrial capabilities to produce a full range of Silicon Impregnated Silicon Carbide (SiSiC) and Reaction-Bonded Silicon Carbide (RB-SiC), integrating precision casting and furnace technologies under one roof; the Company also upgraded its Total Burner Solutions used in annealing/galvanizing furnaces. During the year, the Company acquired freehold land at Halol, Gujarat, as a strategic step towards long-term growth plans. Digital transformation investments — an in-house-built end-to-end CRM platform, a channel-partner portal and mobile app, and Industry 4.0 technologies across facilities — are described as ongoing operational investments rather than capacity additions.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian economy grew ~7.6% in FY2025-26, with industrial/manufacturing sector growth of around 7%, supporting demand across steel, automotive, general engineering, metal fabrication and construction
- Increasing penetration of power tools and organised retail in tier-2/3 markets is continuing to shift demand from manual applications to power tool accessories
- Competitive intensity in Abrasives expected to remain elevated due to imports and new entrants; volatility in raw material, energy and logistics costs (geopolitical) could influence near-term pricing and margins
- PPS benefits from the China+1 strategy of many industries, GST 2.0 (especially Auto), and PLI support for Electronics, Semiconductors, White Goods and EV; rising adoption of Single Use products in Bio-Pharma (Biologics, Vaccines, Biosimilars) and EV penetration in 2W/3W are additional tailwinds; new trade deals could bring more global Auto/Auto Component customers to use India as a manufacturing hub
- PCR's Petrochemical segment is a strong growth area driven by rising investments in carbon black production, gasification and reforming processes
- SiC demand is driven by growing steel production in India; looking to FY2026-27, geopolitical supply-chain disruptions are expected to increase dependence on local manufacturers, potentially supporting better pricing and operating profit for domestic SiC producers
- FY2026-27 outlook: broadly supportive economic environment led by domestic demand, continued public and private capex, and gradual normalisation of inflation and interest rates, though geopolitical developments, trade actions and commodity/freight price volatility may intermittently impact sentiment
- Company expects healthy demand in core end markets — automotive, steel, infrastructure and general manufacturing — while accelerating expansion in emerging opportunities including electronics, semiconductors, defence and aerospace

risks.risk: Geopolitical demand disruption in PPS end markets
risks.note: Demand disruption due to geopolitical uncertainty in key markets like Automotive, Life Sciences, Industrial and Oil & Gas is flagged as a major short-term risk for the Performance Polymer Solutions business.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and input cost inflation
risks.note: An inflationary environment, concerns over availability of key raw materials, and logistical uncertainties are flagged as critical challenges for the PPS business in the current year; PCR also flags supply chain disruptions and price surcharges on raw materials/energy from ongoing geopolitical tensions.
Depreciation of the Rupee is flagged as a risk specifically because the Performance Polymer Solutions business is import-intensive.

risks.risk: Import competition and pricing pressure across Abrasives and Silicon Carbide
risks.note: The Abrasives business faces margin pressure on key high-margin products from global players entering India and rising Chinese imports (power tools accessory range); the Silicon Carbide business faces competition from imports mainly from China, Vietnam and Russia, which kept market prices subdued and pressured margins/volumes during the year.

risks.risk: Subsidiary performance sensitivity to power/input costs
risks.note: Saint-Gobain Ceramic Materials Bhutan Private Limited (SGCMBPL), the Company's SiC-manufacturing subsidiary, saw its business subdued during the year on account of increased power and input costs.

risks.risk: PCR export decline from geopolitical/tariff risk
risks.note: PCR exports declined during the year due to the uncertain geopolitical situation and the imposition of tariffs in the US.

risks.risk: Structurally limited growth in Digital Services (INDEC) segment
risks.note: The captive IT unit operates on a cost-plus model for the Saint-Gobain Group; management states growth in this segment is limited and future growth can happen only on account of cost inflation, and financial performance may be impacted by foreign exchange fluctuation and hedging strategy.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from new entrants adjacent to Abrasives
risks.note: Paint, Adhesives and similar companies entering the Abrasives market with deep distribution and aggressive pricing have been able to penetrate the market quickly, adding to competitive pressure alongside established European/Japanese niche players and Chinese imports.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Grindwell Norton Limited (GNO), a subsidiary of France's Saint-Gobain group, is the market leader in India's abrasives industry and also operates Performance Polymer Solutions (PPS) and Performance Ceramics and Refractories (PCR) businesses serving steel, automotive, general engineering and …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: GNO manufactures and trades Abrasives (bonded, thin wheels, coated/non-woven, superabrasives, construction products, sealants & adhesives) and, under its Ceramics & Plastics segment, Performance Polymer Solutions (PTFE bearings, seals, life-science tubings, tapes) and Performance Ceramics and Refractories (refractories and engineered ceramics including Silicon Carbide) for customers such as steel, automotive, bearings, general engineering, aerospace, defence, life sciences and construction. It is part of the Saint-Gobain group, drawing on the group's R&D, grain manufacturing (Ceramic Materials Division) and global technology access.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, France — holding: Ultimate holding company, per BRSR and Related Party Transactions disclosure
- Saint-Gobain Ceramic Materials Bhutan Private Limited (SGCMBPL) — subsidiary: 70%-held subsidiary; engaged in manufacture of Silicon Carbide near Phuentsholing, Bhutan; business was subdued during the year on account of increased power and input costs; not a material subsidiary under Regulation 16(1)(c) of Listing Regulations
- Advanced Synthetic Minerals Private Limited (ASMPL) — JV: 49%-held joint venture; during FY2025-26 focused on improving quality and debottlenecking
- Cleanwin Energy Three LLP — associate: 27.27%-held associate; investment for sourcing wind-generated green energy for the Company's Mora Plant, contributing to cost efficiency and sustainability commitments
- Numerous Saint-Gobain group fellow subsidiaries worldwide (e.g. Saint-Gobain India Private Limited, Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics Corporation (US), Saint-Gobain Abrasives entities across China/Thailand/Australia/Europe, Certainteed entities (US/Canada), Saint-Gobain Glass entities (France/UK/Egypt), among many others) — related party: Fellow subsidiaries of ultimate holding company Compagnie de Saint-Gobain, disclosed under Ind AS 24 Related Party Disclosures for related-party transaction purposes

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Abrasives:** Bonded Abrasives, Thin Wheels (Cutting/Grinding Wheels), Coated Abrasives, Non-woven Abrasives, Superabrasives (Diamond/CBN), Construction products, Sealants & Adhesives
- **Performance Polymer Solutions (PPS):** EQYO — PTFE Bearings, Yoke Assemblies, precision injection molding components, Omniseal Solutions — Spring Energized Polymer Seals & Metal Seals, Life Sciences — Silicone/TPE Tubings, Single Use Bags & Assemblies, Tape Solutions — EV Tapes & Foams, Pressure Sensitive Adhesive & Acrylic Foam Tapes, Wire Harness tapes, Performance Film Solutions
- **Performance Ceramics and Refractories (PCR):** Refractory products (Tap Hole Clay, Trough & Runner Castables), Engineered ceramics (Silicon impregnated Silicon Carbide, Reaction-bonded Silicon Carbide), Ceramics for Sanitaryware, Tableware, Ballistic Armour Protection, Wear Resistance Systems

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian economy grew ~7.6% in FY2025-26, with industrial/manufacturing sector growth of around 7%, supporting demand across steel, automotive, general engineering, metal fabrication and construction
- Increasing penetration of power tools and organised retail in tier-2/3 markets is continuing to shift demand from manual applications to power tool accessories
- Competitive intensity in Abrasives expected to remain elevated due to imports and new entrants; volatility in raw material, energy and logistics costs (geopolitical) could influence near-term pricing and margins
- PPS benefits from the China+1 strategy of many industries, GST 2.0 (especially Auto), and PLI support for Electronics, Semiconductors, White Goods and EV; rising adoption of Single Use products in Bio-Pharma (Biologics, Vaccines, Biosimilars) and EV penetration in 2W/3W are additional tailwinds; new trade deals could bring more global Auto/Auto Component customers to use India as a manufacturing hub
- PCR's Petrochemical segment is a strong growth area driven by rising investments in carbon black production, gasification and reforming processes
- SiC demand is driven by growing steel production in India; looking to FY2026-27, geopolitical supply-chain disruptions are expected to increase dependence on local manufacturers, potentially supporting better pricing and operating profit for domestic SiC producers
- FY2026-27 outlook: broadly supportive economic environment led by domestic demand, continued public and private capex, and gradual normalisation of inflation and interest rates, though geopolitical developments, trade actions and commodity/freight price volatility may intermittently impact sentiment
- Company expects healthy demand in core end markets — automotive, steel, infrastructure and general manufacturing — while accelerating expansion in emerging opportunities including electronics, semiconductors, defence and aerospace

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Abrasives: mitigate pressure on key high-margin products from global players entering India by constantly upgrading products and expanding into new markets and segments
- Abrasives: grow non-engineering channels and diversify into adjacency products, while increasing efforts to grow exports, to partially insulate the business from segment-specific volatility
- Abrasives: continue investing in technology, capacities and capabilities to meet growing competitive challenges from Chinese imports, Paint/Adhesives entrants, and European/Japanese niche players
- PPS: fully aligned to Saint-Gobain Group's 'Lead & Grow' strategy, with five focus areas — growing the business by leveraging capacities & capabilities; competency building for breakthrough solutions; building Application & Product Management expertise; focus on cost, efficiency & working capital via new digital tools; and building stronger processes & enablers for service and growth
- PCR (Secondary Steel): maintain leadership via new products, application engineering techniques and business models focused on increasing throughput and reducing melting cost, including the 'Steel Club' customer engagement/training program
- PCR (Petrochemicals): growth strategy centred on consolidating core offers, selectively expanding into ultra-high-temperature applications, and leveraging India-based manufacturing and engineering capabilities; carbon black remains a key focus area
- SiC: focus on maximising output from both manufacturing locations (Tirupati and Bhutan) along with continued emphasis on price improvement and cost control
- Group-wide: diversified portfolio with continued focus on commercial excellence, innovation, cost competitiveness, productivity, digitalisation and sustainability to sustain profitable growth
- Dividend Distribution Policy objective is to appropriately reward shareholders by sharing a portion of profits while retaining sufficient funds for the Company's growth, balancing dividend payout against profit retention for business utilisation. Before declaring/recommending dividend, the Board considers: profit earned during the financial year, capital expenditure requirements, operating cash flows and treasury position, cash retention for exceptional contingencies, acquisitions or new investments requiring higher capital allocation, higher working capital requirements affecting free cash flow, the external economic environment, and the legal/regulatory framework. The Board may declare interim dividends as it considers fit and recommends final dividend for shareholder approval. Retained earnings are utilised based on expansion plans, diversification, and long-term strategic plans.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Abrasives (Coated segment): commissioning of a new paper maker and a new non-woven line increased production capacity and enhanced the ability to customise products to precise customer specifications. Abrasives (Thin Wheel and Bonded segments): investments in capability building and capacity expansion are already yielding an expanded product range and enhanced innovation capabilities. PCR: engineered ceramics manufacturing capabilities at the Halol plant were expanded with new industrial capabilities to produce a full range of Silicon Impregnated Silicon Carbide (SiSiC) and Reaction-Bonded Silicon Carbide (RB-SiC), integrating precision casting and furnace technologies under one roof; the Company also upgraded its Total Burner Solutions used in annealing/galvanizing furnaces. During the year, the Company acquired freehold land at Halol, Gujarat, as a strategic step towards long-term growth plans. Digital transformation investments — an in-house-built end-to-end CRM platform, a channel-partner portal and mobile app, and Industry 4.0 technologies across facilities — are described as ongoing operational investments rather than capacity additions.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership in India's abrasives industry with the widest product range (one of only two full-range players)
- Backward integration via Saint-Gobain's Ceramic Materials Division, which manufactures high-end abrasive grains
- Access to Saint-Gobain's global R&D centres (including a Centre in India) and Centers of Excellence
- Deep customer connect, ability to customise solutions, and brand equity built over decades
- Broad-based industry exposure in Abrasives — dependence on any single industry segment is less than 15%, insulating the business from segment-specific volatility
- Extensive domestic distribution network plus growing non-engineering channels and export diversification
- Digital transformation: in-house-built end-to-end CRM platform, channel partner portal/app, and Industry 4.0 investments improving process efficiency and quality control
- Each PPS sub-business (EQYO, Omniseal Solutions, Life Sciences, Tape Solutions) is a market leader in its space globally and in India

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Geopolitical demand disruption in PPS end markets — Demand disruption due to geopolitical uncertainty in key markets like Automotive, Life Sciences, Industrial and Oil & Gas is flagged as a major short-term risk for the Performance Polymer Solutions business.
- Raw material availability and input cost inflation — An inflationary environment, concerns over availability of key raw materials, and logistical uncertainties are flagged as critical challenges for the PPS business in the current year; PCR also flags supply chain disruptions and price surcharges on raw materials/energy from ongoing geopolitical tensions.
- Currency risk from import intensity — Depreciation of the Rupee is flagged as a risk specifically because the Performance Polymer Solutions business is import-intensive.
- Import competition and pricing pressure across Abrasives and Silicon Carbide — The Abrasives business faces margin pressure on key high-margin products from global players entering India and rising Chinese imports (power tools accessory range); the Silicon Carbide business faces competition from imports mainly from China, Vietnam and Russia, which kept market prices subdued and pressured margins/volumes during the year.
- Subsidiary performance sensitivity to power/input costs — Saint-Gobain Ceramic Materials Bhutan Private Limited (SGCMBPL), the Company's SiC-manufacturing subsidiary, saw its business subdued during the year on account of increased power and input costs.
- PCR export decline from geopolitical/tariff risk — PCR exports declined during the year due to the uncertain geopolitical situation and the imposition of tariffs in the US.
- Structurally limited growth in Digital Services (INDEC) segment — The captive IT unit operates on a cost-plus model for the Saint-Gobain Group; management states growth in this segment is limited and future growth can happen only on account of cost inflation, and financial performance may be impacted by foreign exchange fluctuation and hedging strategy.
- Competitive intensity from new entrants adjacent to Abrasives — Paint, Adhesives and similar companies entering the Abrasives market with deep distribution and aggressive pricing have been able to penetrate the market quickly, adding to competitive pressure alongside established European/Japanese niche players and Chinese imports.
